source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: Algorithm 13.1; proof of Theorem 13.4; Problem 13.1; printed pp. 208, 210, 226 / PDF pp. 220, 222, 238

target: Prove the initial value and exact endpoint update under the printed full history bound.

searched_existing: The shared declaration graph and the pinned Mathlib real Gamma function, its values at 1 and 1/2, its positive recurrence and positivity.
planned_consumers: The endpoint cases of the potential inequality in the proof of Theorem 13.4.
reuse_plan.decision_reason: Both signs use the same scaled Gamma potential and the same two printed range constraints. Each sign increments a different Gamma argument.

semantic_roundtrip.formalizer: Astra / medium formalizer of the KT potential, endpoint recurrence and two consumers.
semantic_roundtrip.blind_decoder: Separate neutral reconstructions of the initial value, endpoint recurrence and two concrete consumers.
semantic_roundtrip.source_reviewer: Independent checks of the printed source, frozen proposition types, full proof expressions, and saturated parent calls in both endpoint instances.
semantic_roundtrip.remaining_semantic_delta: Algorithm 13.1 starts with ε>0. Both identities extend to every real scale ε because the potential is linear in ε.

graph_contribution.functor_reason: The existing real Gamma interface supplies the special-function identities. Both concrete consumers reference the shared potential. Teaching order follows evaluation at t=0 then t≥1. The endpoint theorem uses the shared definition and Gamma recurrences; a teaching route does not supply a formal proof edge from the initial value.
graph_contribution.visual_review: Local candidate preview under review. Final graph traversal follows exact-head validation.

website_surfaces: Online Learning Book, KT endpoint route, source proof steps, shared declaration catalog and Lean Graph.

truth_boundary: Theorem 13.4 also needs a potential inequality for coins strictly between −1 and 1, wealth induction, and a lower estimate for the potential. The endpoint identities supply only the two equalities.

focused_checks: Both private proofs and consumer proofs compiled. Raw public and consumer proposition comparisons and every generated proof difference are recorded in docs/contracts/online-kt-endpoints-v1/proof-attempts.json.
verification.independent_review: The two private theorems have exact frozen proposition types. The independent consumer audit compared both complete types and verified the four saturated calls for the two signs and the two applications of the initial value.

contributor.name: Ji Cheng with Codex assistance
contributor.role: Formalizer with distinct neutral decoder, independent source/body reviewer and independent executor.

salvage.reason: The endpoint proofs compiled. The raw consumer comparator returned 1 and the complete proof-argument differences were retained and adjudicated.

parallelism.expected_information_gain: Check the two endpoint values before using their recurrence in the interior interpolation argument.

cross_route_blind_spot_audit.evidence: The canaries check a non-unit initial scale and both signs at a fractional history; the second test distinguishes the two positive values.
cross_route_blind_spot_audit.canonical_route: Evaluate the Gamma product at time zero and apply the Gamma recurrence for each sign at positive time.
cross_route_blind_spot_audit.selection_reason: One Lean definition represents the scale and both histories.

reader_backpressure.exposition_evidence: Two source cards connect the Gamma identities to the updates. Final reader verification follows the shared project gate.
